clue.text: American poet of sterling worth

definitions.meaning: Ezra, the American modernist poet behind the Cantos
the value of one unit of British currency, a quid

explanation.surface: A tribute to an American writer of real merit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra the modernist poet shares his surname with the British currency unit, whose value is what 'sterling worth' names.

clue.text: The homely fare they have in Lombardy?

definitions.text: The homely fare they have in Lombardy?

parts.words: The homely fare they have in Lombardy?
parts.note: Lombardy lies on the flat Po valley, so food eaten there is food of the flatland, while homely fare is simple cooking

explanation.surface: A question about the simple cooking of a region of northern Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Lombardy sits on the great flat expanse of the Po valley, so its meals are those of the flatland; simple, unfussy cooking carries the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple unadorned cooking is called this, and the Lombard landscape is a level flatland.

clue.text: They get held up when the weather breaks

definitions.text: They get held up when the weather breaks

parts.words: They get held up when the weather breaks
parts.note: held up sounds like delayed or robbed, but here means raised overhead when rain starts

explanation.surface: Travellers delayed when a storm arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain shades are raised above the head once a downpour begins.

clue.text: End up with nothing inwardly accomplished?

indicators.note: inwardly says the nought goes into the middle of the turned word
in a down clue, up says the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Finishing a task with nothing gained inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns END into DNE, and 'inwardly' puts O (nothing) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A task that is accomplished is finished or completed.

clue.text: Dropping in to see someone getting better?

definitions.meaning: paying a call on an acquaintance, as in calling on an old friend
improving, as prospects or trade do

explanation.surface: Visiting a patient who is recovering.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to pay someone a visit and, of a situation, to improve.

clue.text: She finished up with the brand Arthur had

definitions.text: She finished up with the brand Arthur had

parts.words: She finished up with the brand Arthur had
parts.note: brand is an old poetic word for a sword, and in legend King Arthur's sword was returned at last to a watery enchantress

explanation.surface: A woman who ended up owning the brand a man called Arthur used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brand' suggests a trade name but is an old word for a sword: Excalibur, thrown back to the enchantress of the mere at Arthur's death.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian legend the enchantress of the mere received Excalibur back when the king died.

clue.text: This month's commercial contraction

definitions.meaning: in old business letters, of the current month
a shortened form used in trade correspondence

explanation.surface: A note on a business abbreviation for the current month.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for instant, it was the clerk's shorthand in letters for the present month, as in 'yours of the 5th'.

clue.text: Government proposals for preserving the countryside?

definitions.meaning: a consultation document issued by a British ministry before legislation
a document that is eco-friendly, written by environmentalists

explanation.surface: Official plans to protect rural Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a consultative document setting out the government's proposals is named for its cover colour; that colour also means environmental.
explanation.definitionFit: A British consultative document carries this colour name, and the colour also stands for environmentalism.

clue.text: See 6
White vestment put on an early martyr

parts.note: an alb is the white linen robe worn by a priest
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dressing a saint in white robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' just joins the robe to AN. Saint Alban was the first British Christian martyr.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Alban was Britain's first recorded Christian martyr, killed in Roman times.

clue.text: Profoundly enjoyed retirement?

parts.note: retirement here is going to bed, and profoundly means soundly, at depth

explanation.surface: A pensioner who has relished leaving work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' looks like leaving work but means retiring to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound, heavy slumber is what someone who has gone to bed enjoys profoundly.

clue.text: Compassionate mission

parts.note: a journey undertaken out of kindness to help someone in need

explanation.definitionFit: A kindly journey to give help or relief is a compassionate mission.

clue.text: Bill's political opponents

parts.note: the members who vote against a parliamentary bill

explanation.surface: The rivals of a politician named Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is a parliamentary bill; those voting against it in the division lobby are counted as this group.
explanation.definitionFit: In a parliamentary division the votes against a measure are tallied under this name.

clue.text: Get on a governing body

definitions.meaning: to climb aboard a ship, train or bus
a committee of directors running an organisation

explanation.surface: Advice to join a committee that runs things.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for embarking and a noun for a firm's directors.

clue.text: A singularly heavy blow?

parts.note: singularly hints at a single unit, and a knockout punch can be called by a word built from the number

explanation.surface: An exceptionally hard punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singularly' reads as 'remarkably' but points to the number one; colloquial British English calls a single decisive blow this.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a punch that settles things in a single go, also any one-of-a-kind thing.

clue.text: Mogul city in which there's nothing but a Greek marketplace

indicators.note: in which there's says the city holds the nought inside it

parts.note: Agra, the Indian city of the Taj Mahal, was a Mughal capital
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An Indian imperial city that turns out to contain only an ancient Greek market.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greek cities the public assembly place and market square bore this name.

clue.text: The flower of fictional detectives?

parts.note: flower suggests the finest of the bunch, but means a garden plant that shares its name with a famous French fictional gentleman thief

explanation.surface: Naming the finest detective in fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' reads as 'the best of', but means a plant; Arsène, Maurice Leblanc's gentleman burglar who also turns sleuth, has the plant's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall garden plant with spikes of pea-like blooms shares its name with Leblanc's gentleman thief.

clue.text: The manufacture of electric bulbs, for instance

definitions.text: The manufacture of electric bulbs, for instance

parts.words: The manufacture of electric bulbs, for instance
parts.note: making lamps is a business producing illumination, and small-scale consumer production has the same name

explanation.surface: An example of a factory process.
explanation.walkthrough: Small-scale consumer manufacturing has a name which, read literally, means a trade producing lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-scale production of consumer goods is so called; read literally, it is an illumination business.

clue.text: Unruly daughters of whom the Army is proud?

definitions.text: of whom the Army is proud?

indicators.note: unruly says the letters of the next word are out of order

explanation.surface: Wayward girls who nonetheless make the military proud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unruly' rearranges DAUGHTERS. The Guards are the British Army's elite household regiments.
explanation.definitionFit: The household regiments of the British Army are its prestige troops, the pride of the service.

clue.text: Cathy's new fellow? Marina provides for him

indicators.note: new says the letters of Cathy's are made over in a fresh order

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A woman's new boyfriend, whom someone called Marina looks after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marina' looks like a woman's name but is a harbour for small boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a harbour for pleasure boats, so it serves the sailor who owns one.

clue.text: Are important enough to merit critical review?

definitions.meaning: warrant attention
earn a write-up from a critic

explanation.surface: Asking whether a new work is significant enough for a reviewer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to warrant attention, and literally to earn a critic's write-up.

clue.text: A bad habit that's not easy to get out of

definitions.meaning: a moral failing or indulgence

definitions.text: that's not easy to get out of
definitions.meaning: a bench clamp with jaws that grip tightly

explanation.surface: A warning about a habit hard to break.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a moral failing and a workshop clamp whose jaws hold tight.

clue.text: It follows 6' scall

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'It follows 6' scall (5)', garbled by OCR; no scan or search gives the printed text

clue.text: Go after work as an engraver?

definitions.meaning: pursue
to engrave or emboss metal

explanation.surface: Pursuing a career in engraving.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to pursue, and also to decorate metal by engraving or embossing.

clue.text: Grievously harms the object in writing?

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed within another

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
aims are objects or goals

explanation.surface: Objecting to cruelty in written work.
explanation.definitionFit: To maim is to injure badly, so this verb means wounds grievously.

clue.text: Precisely what the verdict should be

definitions.meaning: exactly
fair and right, as a court's ruling ought to be

explanation.surface: A remark on what a jury ought to deliver.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both 'exactly' and fair or rightful, as a ruling ought to be.

clue.text: A woebegone expression

parts.note: expression reads as a look on a face, but is an exclamation of sorrow

explanation.walkthrough: 'expression' looks like a facial look but is an exclamation of grief.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of grief or regret is a sorrowful utterance.

clue.text: Bogus feature of a famous hamlet

indicators.note: feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Doubting a village's claimed fame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamlet' tempts thoughts of Shakespeare, but it is just a village whose letters hold the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bogus is fake, a pretence.

clue.text: A pony, perhaps, that doesn't count for much

definitions.meaning: in Britain a pony is a small glass of beer
something trivial or unimportant

explanation.surface: A small horse treated as unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pony' looks like a horse but in British pubs is a small measure of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small measure of ale is literally this, and the phrase also means trivial matters.

clue.text: One who overacts about getting inside a seraglio

indicators.note: getting inside says the word for about goes within the actor

parts.note: a ham is an actor who overplays
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A showy performer sneaking into a sultan's women's quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the women's quarters of a Muslim household, a Turkish word for the same place.

clue.text: Seeking universal brotherhood, they shop around erratically

indicators.note: erratically says the letters are thrown into a disordered arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
around read as 'a round', a ring shape giving O

explanation.surface: People browsing around shops with no plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is read as 'a round', the ring-shaped O, which joins the anagram fodder that 'erratically' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Theosophical Society's first aim was to form a nucleus of universal human brotherhood.

clue.text: Constructive member of society

parts.note: constructive suggests helpful, but means building with stone; society is a fraternal lodge

explanation.surface: A praiseworthy citizen who contributes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constructive' means building, and the society is the Freemasons.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoneworker builds, and a Freemason belongs to a fraternal society, so both senses fit.
